topic: Perfect Forwarding and Universal References in STL Containers
explanation: Perfect forwarding allows a function template to forward its arguments to another function without unnecessary copies or conversions, preserving the original argument's value category (lvalue or rvalue).  This is achieved through universal references, which are references that can bind to both lvalues and rvalues.  The compiler's implementation leverages template argument deduction and reference collapsing rules to determine the appropriate forwarding mechanism.  This impacts both compile-time behavior (template instantiation) and runtime behavior (function call efficiency).  Failure to correctly understand perfect forwarding can lead to performance bottlenecks due to unnecessary copies or moves, or subtle bugs due to incorrect argument forwarding.
keywords: Perfect Forwarding, Universal References, std::forward, Forwarding References
